chapter: Cab Calloway, Harlem and New York musicians
title: Piano players in fish bars, speakeasies and rent parties
summary: Danny says pianists once had the supper-club and speakeasy gigs, and Milt describes Chicago house rent parties.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: You want to tell them about the fish bar, Danny? Your experiences in them fish bars? (?) those piano players?
We didn't have too many piano players playing fish bars, Smitty.
In my time, of course, the piano players had all the gigs. Even in a lot of the speakeasies they had a lot of the gigs. Just piano players alone. And they'd open ...(?)... what they called suppers.
Oh, yeah. Well, when they got to Chicago, there was house rent parties and things.
Same thing, they just called it different, you know. People supplement the rent. If they have a little trouble or the money is short, they'd give a party and invite all their friends.

The most personable ones became landladies. And they had enough charisma to attract attention, and they were very popular -- served some good booze and kept some nice ladies around in their apartments. Somebody could come by...
